title.suggested: St. Louis' First Title Fight, 68 Years Ago

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch's John E. Wray retold Tom Allen's 1869 fight with Mike McCoole, lost on an intimidated referee's decision, and his 1873 win over McCoole on Chouteau Island, which the paper called St. Louis' first world title fight.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Sunday Morning, March 30, 1941, pages 13A and 14A. The article says Allen died in 1904 at age 64; he died in 1903.

facts.fact: Allen and Mike McCoole first fought in 1869 on Foster's Island in the Mississippi, not far from St. Louis, admittedly for the American title
places: Foster's Island, Mississippi River, near St. Louis

facts.fact: In the 1869 fight a mob of McCoole supporters slashed the ropes and rushed the referee with knives and revolvers in the ninth round; that night, from the stage of the Casino Theater, referee Valentine McKinney gave the decision to McCoole on a foul, saying Allen had gouged his eye

Allen beat McCoole on Sept. 23, 1873, on Chouteau Island (now part of the Illinois mainland at East St. Louis), in 16 minutes and seven rounds, when McCoole's second Tom Kelly threw in the towel; the fight was billed for the world title
places: Chouteau Island, Mississippi River, near East St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen to McCoole's second during the 1873 fight, as the 1941 article quotes him
facts.quote: It's a shame to keep such a man before me. Take him out!

facts.fact: At 37, Allen lost the championship to Joe Goss in 21 rounds on a foul and then retired
After retiring, Allen named his saloon on Market near Seventh Street "Champion's Rest"; the photo caption puts it where the American Hotel later stood
places: Market Street near Seventh, St. Louis
